Judgment:

The present appeal is filed by the Appellant/New India Insurance Company Limited, aggrieved by the Order dated 11.07.2019 passed in M.V.O.P.No.836 of 2014 on the file of the Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-Cum-VII Additional District and Sessions Judge, Eluru, West Godavari.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-Cum-VII Additional District and Sessions Judge, Eluru, West Godavari

sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri K.Jagadishwar, learned counsel representing Sri T.V.P. Sai Vihari for the appellant and Sri P.Shiva Prasad, learned counsel representing Sri Eluru Sesha Mahesh Babu for the respondent Nos.1 to 4.
3.

The facts leading to the case on hand are as follows:
On 31.05.2015 at 10:30 AM, the deceased by name Vemula Anjaneyulu @ David Raju along with his wife was going to Vijayawada on his motor cycle bearing Registration No. AP 16 BN 5865 to see his elder son, who was studying in Sri Medha College at Vijayawada.

It is the further case of the claimants that the brother- in-law of the deceased was coming on a separate motorcycle behind the deceased and when they reached Gopalapuram Village at NRI College, a mini lorry bearing Registration No.
AP 16 TX 6949 came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed in opposite direction and dashed the motorcycle of the deceased.
As a result of which, the deceased fell down on the road and sustained severe head injury and died on the spot.
A case was registered in Crime No.69 of 2012 under Section 304(A) of IPC and Sections 180 & 181 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

The wife along with her children and the mother of the deceased filed petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.7,00,000/- with interest @ 12% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realization for the death of the deceased.
The driver, cleaner and the owner of the vehicle remained ex-parte before the Tribunal.
The 4th respondent/ appellant/ insurance company alone contested the claim.
The 4th respondent/ insurance company filed counter-affidavit denying all the averments made in the claim petition.

It was pleaded by the 4th respondent/ insurance company that at the time of the accident, the vehicle was driven by the 2nd respondent/
cleaner, who did not possess any driving license and thereby, the 3rd respondent/
owner committed violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

It is specifically pleaded that as the 3rd respondent/owner allowed the 2nd respondent/
New India Assurance Company Limited vs Vemula Rajamani on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196531425/
3 cleaner to drive the vehicle, therefore, the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation as claimed and pleaded to exonerate from liability.

sentences.text: It is further contended that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the deceased.

4. In order to prove the case of the claimants, they have examined P.Ws.1 and 2 and marked Exs.A1 to A9.
5.
On the other hand, the 4th respondent/insurance company has examined R.W.1 and marked Exs.B1 to B5.

Upon consideration of the oral and documentary evidence put forth by the parties, the Tribunal allowed the claim petition by granting compensation of Rs.8,29,375/- conventional on various heads along with costs and interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of the petition till realization.
6. Aggrieved the said Award, the 4th respondent/ insurance company preferred the present appeal.

The only ground of challenge is that the 4th respondent/ appellant/ insurance company is not liable to pay compensation in as much as there is violation of terms and conditions of the policy by the 3rd respondent/ owner.
The appellant did not dispute with regard to the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
7. In view of the same, this Court is not inclined to go into the quantum of the Award.

It is a specific case of the insurance company/ appellant that the vehicle was driven by the 2nd respondent/
cleaner and at the time of the accident, he did not possess valid driving license.
In order to prove its case, R.W.1/ employee of the appellant/ insurance company was examined.

8. On perusal of the deposition of the R.W.1, except reiterating the contents of the counter-affidavit,
nothing is placed on record to substantiate that at the time of accident, the 2nd respondent/cleaner was driving the offending vehicle.
9. It is needless to mention that the burden of proof lies on the insurance company to establish that the terms and conditions of the policy have been breached by the insured.

As already noted supra,
when R.W.1 was examined on behalf of the appellant, except marking the copy of the insurance policy of the offending vehicle, nothing is placed on record to show that the terms and conditions have been violated by the 3rd respondent/ owner of the offending vehicle.

10. In the absence of any evidence, the contention of the appellant company cannot be countenanced and the same is rejected as the appellant/ insurance company failed to prove that the vehicle was driven by the cleaner of the vehicle.
11. In the circumstances, this Court has no hesitation to hold that the question of exonerating the appellants from the liability does not arise.

Further, though it is contended by the learned counsel for the appellant that a direction may be given to the insurance company to pay and recover from the 3rd respondent, in view of the fact that the appellant company failed to establish that the 3rd respondent has violated the terms and conditions of the policy, the request of the appellant cannot New India Assurance Company Limited vs Vemula Rajamani on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196531425/
4 be considered and the same is hereby rejected.
